Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get you a recommended deployment and high-level sizing: 

Recap (what I heard):
- Primary workload: real-time triage assistant for clinicians.
- Expected peak traffic: ~1,000 requests/sec (spiky around shift changes).
- Typical response size: ~40 tokens (avg), some sessions up to 200 tokens.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 100ms is ideal; p99 <= 250ms is a hard requirement for patient-facing flows.
- Security: you said data residency in US, and no strict need for on-prem initially — hosted or dedicated acceptable.

Questions to confirm before we size:
1) Is 1,000 req/sec the true instantaneous peak (QPS) or is that sustained over a minute? Any concurrency pattern (bursts)?
2) Will inference be stateless per request, or are you using long-running sessions with KV cache (conversation state)?
3) Any regulatory constraints that would push this to Private (VPC/on-prem) instead of Dedicated?

Why this matters: Hosted API can get you started quickly and handle most bursts, but for predictable p95/p99 at 1k QPS we typically recommend Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor variability and get lower tail latency. Dedicated also simplifies throughput guarantees for SLAs.

Next steps I propose:
- You answer the three quick Qs above.
- If confirmed, we’ll have one of our SEs (cc'd) put together a Dedicated sizing estimate (nodes, GPU class, expected throughput/latency and cost delta vs hosted).
- Optionally run a quick canary on Hosted to validate the p50/p95 with a representative payload before committing.

I attached the call notes template and our sizing checklist.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if helpful.

Hi Susan / Marissa —

Thanks for the context — quick technical read and recommendation based on the bursty 1k instantaneous QPS and ~40-token payloads. I’ll keep this high level; happy to dive deeper on a call.

Sizing (ballpark):
- Recommendation: Dedicated reserved capacity for production to meet p95/p99 SLAs with predictable tails. Hosted can work for functional validation and early canary traffic.
- Baseline Dedicated footprint: 4 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent: 8 x T4-scale nodes depending on instance class).
  - Expected throughput per A100-equivalent node (40-token avg): ~300–400 rps sustained with p95 in the ~40–80ms range; p99 ~120–220ms depending on queuing and prefix/cache hit rates.
  - With 4 nodes, we estimate headroom for 1k instantaneous with short bursts; recommend autoscale + burst reserve (additional node pool) for larger sustained growth.

Latency/cost tradeoffs:
- Hosted: lower time-to-market and no infra commitment. For 1k bursts you’ll likely see higher p95/p99 variance during noisy-neighbor events; cost is pay-as-you-go but per-unit compute can be higher at scale. Good for canary/testing.
- Dedicated: higher predictability and usually lower unit cost at sustained scale. Expect a material monthly delta vs Hosted (ballpark: Dedicated baseline ~2.5x–3x the hosted run-rate for equivalent sustained QPS, but with lower tail latency and reserved capacity guarantees). I’ll provide a more precise example in the sizing doc.

Next actions I need from Acme to finalize numbers:
1) Sample request/response payload or a 30–60 second captures of typical requests so we can validate token counts and any custom ops.
2) Preferred window to run a controlled load test (we can run a canary on Hosted, then a dedicated load test once size is agreed).

If you’re available, I can share a short slide with the node-level math and cost comparison by EOD tomorrow. In parallel we can schedule a 30-minute sizing review next week.
